messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv_cache_paging spike in us-west-2 for model rwinf-awq-7b. 78% paging on cg-3, sustained for 4m. metric: kv_size_bytes up ~4x vs baseline. severity: P1.

sam (oncall): seeing the alert now, pulling up dashboards. any customer-facing errors? :eyes:

jess (support): bumped from customers — several timeout 504s on chat endpoints, about 12 customers, 3 enterprise customers with high priority. No major data loss reported.

maria (eng-runtime): quick hypothesis: recent kernel selector change routed AWQ quantized variants to the new int8 kernel which appears to inflate KV footprint for long context. Continuous batching + prefix caching might be multiplying KV allocations.

kevin (eng-ml): we shipped a fallback change earlier this week for awq->int8 path to test the new kernel. KV per-token size for AWQ went from ~2.1MB to ~8.7MB for long contexts in our repro. this matches the 4x.

lucas (eng-sre): immediate mitigation options? can we force kernel fallback on prod nodes or throttle batching?

maria (eng-runtime): two quick mitigations: 1) temp force kernel selector to `fp16`/existing kernel for that model family; 2) lower continuous batching window and reduce max_batch_size for cg-3. both are low-risk.

sam (oncall): prioritize 1 then 2. maria, can you push the kernel selector rollback?

maria (eng-runtime): performing patch now. will apply `--kernel-preference=fp16` to routing policy for rwinf-awq-7b in us-west-2.

deploy-bot: deploy started by maria at 2026-03-15T15:12:40Z for service: runtime-router, change: force-kernel-fallback-for-awq.

maria (eng-runtime): rolled config to 4 nodes in cg-3 (canary), watching metrics.

lucas (eng-sre): decreasing continuous batching window from 200ms -> 50ms and max_batch_size 64 -> 32 for cg-3. applying now.

deploy-bot: config update applied to cg-3: batching.window_ms=50, batching.max_size=32.

sam (oncall): metric check in 2m. if paging drops, we rollout to remaining nodes.

(2m pass)

lucas (eng-sre): kv paging down to 23% on canary nodes, overall cluster avg dropped from 78% -> 31%. latency tail improved ~180ms.

jess (support): customer reports: errors decreased, a few timeouts still in queuing buckets but major ones resolved. notifying the 3 enterprise accounts.

kevin (eng-ml): confirmed: KV per-token size back to ~2.3MB on canary nodes. looks like kernel selection was the root cause.

maria (eng-runtime): starting rollout to all cg-3 nodes with the kernel fallback. plan: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 12m, maintaining batching throttle.

sam (oncall): doing controlled rollout. monitoring SLOs and paging.

(rollout)

lucas (eng-sre): full rollout complete. cluster paging stable at 18-25%. continuous batching rollback kept.

maria (eng-runtime): creating hotfix PR for kernel selector logic to add safe guard: avoid int8 kernel selection for AWQ variants when context_length > 1024 or when estimated_kv > X. will include telemetry to detect KV blowups earlier.

kevin (eng-ml): plan to add a micro-benchmark that simulates long-prefix AWQ contexts to validate kernel choices pre-rollout.

aaron (eng-platform): note: patch required in autoscaler to account for transient KV growth - otherwise scale decisions oscillate. filing follow-up.

jess (support): sending customer incident notifications now. draft message attached: "We experienced degraded performance impacting some chat requests; mitigation applied; follow-up postmortem forthcoming."

sam (oncall): summary for handoff: root cause = kernel selector choosing int8 kernel for AWQ -> KV footprint spike with continuous batching -> paging and increased tail latencies. Immediate mitigation = force fp16 kernel + reduce batching. Hotfix = kernel selector guard + benchmark coverage + autoscaler tweak.

maria (eng-runtime): will own hotfix PR and postmortem. kevin will own ML regression tests. lucas will own rollout/alert tuning. aaron will update autoscaler. jess will keep customers updated.

sam (oncall): handing off to lucas for next shift. if anything else flares, escalate to oncall-sre. :thumbsup:

lucas (eng-sre): picked up. saving traces and KV heap dumps to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2298765432/ for postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated. severity downgraded to P2. started postmortem tracking ticket: PMT-2298.

maria (eng-runtime): quick notes for postmortem: include reproducer commands, kernel selector diff, canary metrics, customer impact list, and timeline.

kevin (eng-ml): adding model-specific notes: AWQ quant packer increases per-layer kv encoding size under current int8 kernel; need to evaluate AWQ->gptq path differences too.

jess (support): logged affected customer IDs: C-1042, C-1190, C-2015. sent targeted emails.

sam (oncall): closing active mitigation. handoff complete.

(End of thread)
